body:
## Problem

The ISTEX access token lives unexported in `~/.config/keys/istex.env`
(`ISTEX_ACCESSTOKEN=...`). `_get_token()` only read `os.environ`, so
`fetch_istex` failed with "ISTEX_ACCESSTOKEN not set" unless the caller
had sourced the file into the environment first.

## Fix

`_get_token()` now falls back to parsing the `KEY=VALUE` key file when
the environment variable is unset (env var still takes precedence). The
path is a module constant `TOKEN_FILE` so tests can redirect it.

## Tests

- `test_missing_token_fails` now points `TOKEN_FILE` at an absent file so
  it no longer depends on the host's real key.
- New `test_token_read_from_file` covers the file fallback path.
- All 6 tests pass; ruff format + check clean.

Verified end-to-end: with no env var set, `_get_token()` reads the token
from the configured file.

Ticket: none

Rationale:
A 45-line, two-file change with a single clear purpose: read the ISTEX token
from the unexported `~/.config/keys/istex.env` file when the env var is unset,
env var keeping precedence. The parser handles the `export ` prefix, first-`=`
split, and quote stripping, and correctly ignores comment lines. `TOKEN_FILE`
is a redirectable module constant, so both tests are host-independent. No
credential is logged. One non-blocking `consider:`: inline comments trailing a
value are not stripped, which does not occur in real key files. Every stated

commits.messageBody:
The token lives unexported in ~/.config/keys/istex.env; _get_token()
only consulted os.environ, so fetches failed with "ISTEX_ACCESSTOKEN
not set" unless the caller had sourced the file. Fall back to parsing
that KEY=VALUE file (env var still wins) so the fetcher works out of
the box on the configured machine.

Chose a module-level TOKEN_FILE constant over hardcoding the path
inline so tests can redirect it; test_missing_token_fails now points
it at an absent file so it no longer depends on the host's real key.
